vulnerabilities.description: IO::Uncompress::Unzip versions before 2.215 for Perl propagate an uncaught exception when parsing a zip header with a malformed DOS date. The _dosToUnixTime() function calls Time::Local::timelocal() without an eval guard; a header whose date field decodes to an out-of-range month, day, or hour causes the exception to propagate out of the caller, which expects undef plus an error variable instead.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase never invokes Perl or any Perl module.

ratings.justification: Liquibase's container entrypoint execs only the Liquibase Java CLI directly; no Perl interpreter or module is ever invoked.

analysis.detail: Perl's IO::Uncompress::Unzip propagates an uncaught exception when a zip header's DOS date field decodes to an out-of-range value. The container's entrypoint execs only the Liquibase CLI directly (a Java process, not a shell script that shells out to Perl), and a source review found no invocation of perl or any Perl module anywhere in Liquibase's build or runtime. This OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image tag resolves to at build time. Confirmed by pulling the current base image directly and checking installed package versions (not from repo-pinned config), it ships perl-base 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.4, the fixed release, as additional defense-in-depth.

vulnerabilities.description: Socket versions before 2.041 for Perl have an out-of-bounds heap read. pack_ip_mreq_source() in Socket.xs validates argument lengths in the wrong order, so a source address shorter than 4 bytes is not rejected and the copy reads up to 3 bytes past the end of its buffer, leaking adjacent heap memory into the packed structure.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase never invokes Perl or any Perl module.

ratings.justification: Liquibase's container entrypoint execs only the Liquibase Java CLI directly; no Perl interpreter or module is ever invoked.

analysis.detail: An out-of-bounds heap read exists in Perl's Socket module (pack_ip_mreq_source() in Socket.xs) when an application calls it with a multicast source address shorter than 4 bytes. Liquibase never invokes Perl or any Perl module (see the CVE-2025-15649 assessment on this same subcomponent for the reachability evidence). This OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image tag resolves to at build time. Confirmed by pulling the current base image directly and checking installed package versions (not from repo-pinned config), it ships perl-base 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.4, the fixed release, as additional defense-in-depth.

vulnerabilities.description: Perl through version 5.43.9 has a regex overflow flaw. When an alternation compiled into a trie by Perl_study_chunk contains more than 65,535 branches, a 16-bit delta field overflows and the trie's match decision table is silently truncated with no warning, causing the regex to return both false positives and false negatives.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase never invokes Perl, and no Liquibase security control is implemented via a Perl regex.

ratings.justification: Liquibase's container entrypoint execs only the Liquibase Java CLI directly; no Perl interpreter or module is ever invoked, and no Liquibase access-control or filtering logic is implemented via a Perl regex.

analysis.detail: Perl's regex compiler silently truncates its match table when an alternation has more than 65,535 branches, producing incorrect (false-positive and false-negative) pattern matches — a risk only when such a regex gates an access-control or input-filtering decision. Liquibase never invokes Perl or any Perl module (see the CVE-2025-15649 assessment on this same subcomponent for the reachability evidence), so no Liquibase security control is implemented via a Perl regex. This OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image tag resolves to at build time. Confirmed by pulling the current base image directly and checking installed package versions (not from repo-pinned config), it ships perl-base 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.4, the fixed release, as additional defense-in-depth.

vulnerabilities.description: Perl versions through 5.45.1 have out-of-bounds heap reads and writes during regular expression matching via an undersized superlinear cache in S_regmatch. A caller that matches an attacker-controlled subject of the required size and pattern shape can crash the process or corrupt heap memory.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not invoke Perl or Perl regex processing at runtime.

ratings.justification: Liquibase's container entrypoint execs the Java CLI directly; no Perl interpreter or Perl regex engine is invoked.

analysis.detail: This regex-engine heap read/write flaw is reachable only when an application performs Perl regular-expression matching on attacker supplied subject strings. The container entrypoint execs only the Liquibase Java CLI directly (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8`, `docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119`), and a focused grep across the runtime Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no perl invocation. The vulnerable Perl regex path is therefore not reachable from the stock Liquibase Secure runtime.

vulnerabilities.description: Perl versions from 5.9.4 before 5.41.9 can produce incorrect regular expression match results when a stale failure flag ends the Aho-Corasick prescan early in S_find_byclass, which can make access or filtering decisions wrong.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not invoke Perl or make runtime decisions via Perl regex evaluation.

ratings.justification: Liquibase's container entrypoint execs the Java CLI directly; no Perl interpreter or Perl regex engine is invoked.

analysis.detail: This incorrect-match issue affects Perl's regex prescan logic and is relevant only when an application performs Perl regular-expression matching on attacker-controlled data and then makes a security decision from the result. The container entrypoint execs only the Liquibase Java CLI directly (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8`, `docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119`), and a focused grep across the runtime Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no perl invocation. The vulnerable Perl regex path is not reachable in the stock runtime.

vulnerabilities.description: Pod::Text versions before 6.1.1 for Perl allow CPU and memory exhaustion formatting a POD document whose =over nesting drives the margin to the output width. Each =over adds its indent to the margin, which wrap() subtracts from the output width to get the space available for text. When that space reaches zero, the line-splitting substitution matches the empty string, and the loop consumes no input while appending the margin padding on every pass. Formatting an attacker-supplied POD document never returns, and the output grows until memory is exhausted.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. perl is not invoked at container runtime.

ratings.justification: No perl invocation exists anywhere in this image's runtime code path.

analysis.detail: Pod::Text (bundled with perl-base) CPU/memory exhaustion formatting a crafted POD document. Nothing in this repository or docker-entrypoint.sh shells out to perl or invokes POD formatting (pod2text/perldoc); the entrypoint does its own pattern matching with bash case/glob syntax.
